memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'While you plant during the eighth year, you will eat from the old crop
and will continue to eat from it until the harvest of the ninth year comes
in'" - Lev 25:22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The provision from the sixth year did not run out the moment the Sabbath
year ended. It stretched on — through the eighth year of planting, right up
until the ninth year's harvest was gathered. God's supply lasted longer
than they expected.

There is real tenderness in this detail. God did not provide the bare
minimum and then leave them scrambling. He provided with margin, with
extra, with enough to carry them comfortably into the next season.

Dear reader, we often expect God's provision to be tight and last-minute,
just enough to survive. Sometimes it is. But Scripture also shows a God who
provides generously and beyond the immediate need.

Think of the feeding of the five thousand. Jesus did not provide exactly
enough; there were twelve baskets left over (Matt 14:20). The wine at Cana
was not a modest amount but abundant and excellent (John 2:6-10).

We must never turn this into a promise of luxury — that would distort it.
But we can trust the generosity of God's character. Paul says God is able to
do immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine (Eph 3:20).

Look back over your life. Has God's provision not often stretched further
than you feared it would?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I underestimated the generosity of God's provision?
2. When has God's supply lasted longer than I expected?
3. Am I trusting Him for the season ahead, not just today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that Your provision often reaches further than I fear.
Help me trust Your generous heart and rest in Your care for the days
ahead. Amen.
